how: Each clip was watched and listened to in full at normal speed by a person, after the automated checks had passed, comparing what is said with the burned-in captions and the SRT. Round 1 covered every clip. Round 2 re-checked every clip, with a list of the spots changed since round 1: the timing of the highlighted word, the words added under the verbatim rule, and the first seconds of audio.

findings.found: Jerky jump cut, with a lone "we" after it
findings.fix: Cut moved into the pause before "et cetera"; in round 2 the reviewer re-cut it by hand (see round 2)

findings.found: "is" lit up while Effie pauses on "blockchain", before she says it
findings.fix: Word timing by forced alignment of the subtitle text to the audio; "is" now lights up when it is said, after the pause

findings.found: "There is" starts the moment the video starts
findings.fix: 0.4 s silent beat on the speaker's first frame before "There is limited use"

findings.found: Subtitle "right? And I think"; the speaker says "right? So I think"
findings.fix: "right? So, and I think": the reviewer's "So", plus a short "and" that four models hear
"there is a this, this, this person" ("this" is said three times)

findings.found: "to" missing in "we could show to via Tokeniser"
The reviewer re-cut this edit by hand (CapCut), joining "and in our wallets," directly to "we generally tend to" and dropping "et cetera"
findings.fix: Ranges 2 and 3 updated to the new cut (43:20.8-43:28.8, 43:40.5-43:49.8). The reviewer's file was HEVC, so it was transcoded to H.264 (every frame at 49.9 dB PSNR or better against the reviewer's file, same audio), and the SRT was re-timed to the new cut after the watch
